angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 161,402 km at 25.35 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 39.4467 +/- 0.0136 mas (same row, RUWE 1.28): 25.35 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.232 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Lacedelli et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-771 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...698A.223L/abstract): 161,402 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.22 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Lacedelli et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-771 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...698A.223L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3370 +/- 100 K from Lacedelli et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-771 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...698A.223L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lacedelli et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-771 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...698A.223L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-771.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.050, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
